key_insight: SPARKLING makes it possible to stably expand model width in the middle of training by jointly preserving forward/backward signal magnitudes and applying controlled symmetry breaking, enabling width-progressive learning without catastrophic instability.
problem_solved: Addresses the severe training instabilities that occur when increasing model width mid-training—instabilities that have prevented practical width-progressive schedules and limited pre-training compute savings.
method: Signal-preserving layer surgery: add parameters with rescaling/initialization that maintain activation and gradient magnitudes after widening.
Controlled symmetry breaking: introduce small, structured perturbations or asymmetric initialization for new units to avoid neuron collapse and encourage diversity.
Training-state-aware transfer: adapt optimizer state or selectively reset/update moments so training continues smoothly after width changes.
impact: Enables large compute savings and more flexible scaling schedules by allowing safe mid-stage widening—practitioners can progressively widen models with less tuning and fewer stability failures, making large-scale pre-training more efficient.
visual_elements: Training timeline: stages showing when width is expanded and corresponding compute saved (bar/area chart).
Stability comparison: loss and gradient-norm curves for naive widening vs SPARKLING (before/after plots).
Layer diagram: schematic of adding units with rescaling (signal preservation) and small perturbations (symmetry breaking).
Compute vs accuracy curve: shows similar final performance with less pre-training compute when using width-progressive SPARKLING.
paper_title: SPARKLING: Balancing Signal Preservation and Symmetry Breaking for Width-Progressive Learning
paper_authors: Qifan Yu, Xinyu Ma, Zhijian Zhuo, Minrui Wang, Deyi Liu
